info.title: Piro API
info.description: REST API for Piro — an open-source status page platform. Authenticate using a JWT Bearer token (obtained from `/api/v1/auth/sign-in`) or an API key passed in the `X-API-Key` header.

get.summary: Returns all alert configs for the given check.

post.summary: Creates a new alert config on the check.

get.summary: Returns a single alert config by id.

put.summary: Updates an existing alert config.

get.summary:
Returns a paginated list of Alerts (active and historical). Active alerts always sort
before resolved ones, then most-recently-fired first. Optionally filter by FiredAt range.
Returns the full detail of a single Alert, including the AlertConfig criteria that fired it.
Returns all open incidents — for the "attach to incident" picker on an alert.
Returns the full on-call delivery history for this alert's escalation, most recent first.

post.summary:
Links this alert to an incident — creates a new one if `incidentId` is omitted, or
attaches to the given existing incident. Always an explicit, manual action.
Acknowledges an alert, pausing its on-call escalation.

get.summary:
Data-retention preview: how many resolved, non-incident-linked alerts would be deleted with a
given cutoff. Read-only — does not delete anything. Owner/Admin only.

post.summary:
Data-retention cleanup: permanently deletes resolved alerts resolved before the given cutoff
that are not linked to an incident. Active and incident-linked alerts are always preserved.
Owner/Admin only.
Authenticates with email and password, returns JWT + refresh token.
Invalidates the current refresh token.
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token pair.

Starts password recovery. Always returns 200 to avoid revealing whether an
    account exists. No-op when SSO-only mode is on, the email is unknown, or the account
    is SSO/inactive.
Completes password recovery using a token from the reset email.

get.summary: Returns the authenticated user's profile.

put.summary: Updates the authenticated user's display name and/or color.
Changes the authenticated user's password. Rejects SSO accounts, which have no local password.
Marks the post-setup feature showcase as seen for the authenticated user. Idempotent.

get.summary: Lists API keys for the authenticated user. Owner/Admin only.

post.summary: Creates a new API key. The raw key is returned once and cannot be retrieved again. Owner/Admin only.

delete.summary: Revokes an API key. Owner/Admin only.

get.summary: Returns all checks for the given service.

post.summary: Creates a new check within the service.

get.summary: Returns a single check by its slug.

put.summary: Updates an existing check. Only provided fields are changed.

get.summary: Returns execution log entries for a check. Filter by region and/or ISO 8601 time range.
Returns daily up/down/degraded counts per region for the last N days.

post.summary: Manually triggers an immediate check execution. Useful for testing and on-demand refresh.

Dry-runs a testable check (the Script check) in debug mode: executes the script against the live
target, captures console.log, and returns the raw verdict WITHOUT persisting a datapoint or firing
an alert (RFC 0010 §4.8). The optional body carries candidate config so the operator can test
unsaved edits; an empty body tests the persisted config.

get.summary:
Inbound-token info for a check that receives inbound requests (RFC 0013): the masked token,
last-used time, and the base inbound URL. The raw token is not returned here — only on rotate.

post.summary: Rotates a check's inbound token (RFC 0013) and returns the new raw token + full inbound URL, shown once.

get.summary: Returns all checks across all services with their parent service info.

Returns every registered check type with its display metadata, minimum interval, alert
dimensions, required integration, and reflected config schema. Types with
`requiredIntegrationType != null` need that Integration to exist.

Returns MTTA/MTTR/MTTD, alert noise ratio, and incident/alert breakdowns for a date range.
Defaults to the current calendar month (UTC) when `from`/`to` are omitted.
Returns all services that the given service depends on.

post.summary: Declares a new dependency. Rejects the edge if it would create a cycle.

get.summary: Returns current email configuration. Passwords are masked.

put.summary: Saves email provider configuration. Leave password fields null/empty to keep existing values.

post.summary: Sends a test email to the currently authenticated user.

get.summary:
Returns incidents filtered by filter:
"active" (default) = non-resolved, "all" = everything, "resolved" = only resolved,
or a specific state name: "investigating", "identified", "monitoring".
Requires authentication — returns all incidents regardless of publish state.

post.summary: Creates a new incident and optionally links affected services.

get.summary: Returns a single incident by ID with the full admin view (internal fields included).

put.summary: Updates incident metadata or advances its investigation state.

delete.summary: Deletes an incident and all its timeline events.

get.summary:
Returns a paginated page of an incident's full timeline (all events, any visibility), most
recent first — used for the admin "view full timeline" infinite-scroll flow.

post.summary: Posts an update on an incident and optionally advances its status.

put.summary: Updates the text or visibility of an existing update.

delete.summary: Deletes a single update from an incident's timeline.

post.summary: Acknowledges an incident, marking the current user as the responder.

put.summary: Replaces the full set of affected services for an incident in one call.

post.summary: Links an affected service to an incident.

delete.summary: Removes a service link from an incident.

post.summary: Publishes an incident to the status page. Always a manual, explicit action.
Reverts a published incident back to private, hiding it (and its public comments) from the status page.

get.summary:
Starts the OAuth authorization-code flow for an integration and returns the provider
authorization URL the admin's browser should be sent to.

post.summary:
OAuth callback: exchanges the authorization code for tokens and stores them (encrypted)
against the integration the connection was started for.

get.summary:
The redirect URL the admin must register in the provider's OAuth app — resolved by the backend
(from the site URL) so it's always exactly what the OAuth flow will send, never guessed by the UI.
Returns whether an integration currently has a stored OAuth connection.

post.summary: Disconnects an integration by removing its stored OAuth tokens.

get.summary:
Returns the manifest (category, derived direction, capabilities, ConfigJson schema) for every
registered integration (RFC 0016) — enumerated from the integration registry, reflected from
each integration's ConfigType, so it can't drift from what the code actually deserializes.
Returns every configured Integration, with secret config fields masked.

Discovery — which integration action buttons to render for an object of the given context
(RFC 0012 §4.4). One descriptor per (configured integration × ready action). A not-ready action
is absent, never disabled.

Resolves the runtime options for a dynamic-options field (RFC 0012) — e.g. the connected Jira
account's projects, or the issue types for a chosen project (pass its key as dependsOn).
Pre-fills an action's input dialog for a specific target (RFC 0012 §4.6).

post.summary: Executes a user-initiated integration action and returns the external reference it created (RFC 0012 §4.4).

get.summary:
Returns the outbound external references (e.g. a linked Jira ticket) that integration actions
have created for a local object — Alert/Incident/Maintenance (RFC 0012 §4.5). The detail page
renders these as "🔗 OPS-123" links alongside the action buttons.
Returns the most recent inbound webhook requests for this Integration — RFC 0001 §4.4.

post.summary:
Regenerates this Integration's server-generated fields (e.g. a lost/leaked webhook auth
token) and invalidates the old value immediately. Response's ConfigJson is unmasked, the one
time the new value is visible.

get.summary: Returns next/previous fire time and state for every scheduled job.
Returns a paginated list of application log entries.
Returns all maintenance windows.

post.summary:
Creates a maintenance window.
`RRule` must be a valid iCalendar RRULE string (e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO`).
For a one-time window use `FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1`.
Events are materialized automatically for the next 90 days.

get.summary: Returns a single maintenance window by ID.

put.summary: Updates a maintenance window. Changing the RRULE re-materializes all future events.

delete.summary: Deletes a maintenance window and all its events.

post.summary: Cancels a maintenance window and removes all future scheduled events.
Cancels a single occurrence of a recurring maintenance, leaving the maintenance and its other events untouched.

get.summary: The closed catalog of events a subscription can fire on (RFC 0009 §4.2).
Lists all configured OIDC providers (no client secrets).

put.summary: Creates or updates an OIDC provider configuration.

get.summary: Returns SSO-only mode setting.

put.summary: Enables or disables SSO-only mode (disables password sign-in).

get.summary: Returns OIDC providers enabled for the sign-in page.
Returns whether SSO-only mode is active (used by the sign-in page to hide password form).
Initiates the OIDC authorization code + PKCE flow for the given provider.

post.summary:
SPA callback: exchanges authorization code for Piro tokens and returns JSON.
Called by the Vite SPA after Google redirects to /admin/auth/oidc/callback.

get.summary: The current user's own on-call slots across every schedule they appear in — for their personal calendar.
Whether the current user is on-call right now, and for which schedule.
Lightweight schedule list — name and unique roster only, for pickers that don't need rotation detail.
Returns who is currently on-call for this schedule.
Expands the schedule into Gantt slots for the given time range.

post.summary:
Resolves a draft batch of rotation/override changes into slots and coverage gaps over the
given range, without persisting anything — lets the "Save" button warn about uncovered
windows before the user confirms.

put.summary:
Applies a batch of rotation layer and override changes atomically — either every
operation in the request succeeds, or none of them do. Backs the "Save" button on the
schedule detail page, which lets the user stage several edits before persisting them.

get.summary: Lists all postmortems, newest first.

post.summary: Creates a Draft report and seeds an empty value per active field definition.

get.summary:
Returns the analysis template. By default only active definitions (for rendering an empty editor);
pass includeInactive = true to include deactivated ones (template management).

post.summary: Creates a custom analysis field. Restricted to Owner/Admin (RFC 0005 Phase 3a).

put.summary: Edits a field definition (heading/help/active for any; type only for custom). Owner/Admin only.

delete.summary: Deletes a custom field (or deactivates it if in use). System fields can't be deleted. Owner/Admin only.

put.summary: Reorders the analysis template. Owner/Admin only.

get.summary: Returns a single postmortem with its analysis fields and derived timeline.

put.summary: Updates report metadata and/or its analysis field values.

delete.summary: Deletes a postmortem and its analysis content (referenced incidents are untouched).

post.summary: Publishes a Draft report (internal-only in Phase 1).
Reverts a Published report back to Draft.

get.summary: Downloads the finalized report as a PDF. Only available once the report is Published.

post.summary: Links an incident to a postmortem (N:M "data source").

delete.summary: Removes an incident link from a postmortem.

get.summary: Suggests incidents to link, from those overlapping the report's impact window.

post.summary: Adds an author annotation to the report's timeline.

put.summary: Edits an existing timeline annotation.

get.summary: Returns all maintenance windows with their upcoming events, for the public status page.

Returns published, non-merged incidents for the public status page.
Pass `includeResolved=true` to include incident history.
Returns a single incident by ID, only if it's published — internal fields are always stripped.

Returns a paginated page of a published incident's Public timeline events, most recent first —
used for the "view full timeline" infinite-scroll flow on the public status page.
Returns all visible services with their current computed status.
Returns a single visible service with its current computed status.
Returns uptime percentage for a service over the last `days` days (default 30).

Returns per-day aggregated status and latency data for the service detail page.
Query param: `days` (1–90, default 30).

Returns 1440 minute-aligned status entries for a single day.
All minutes default to UP; minutes covered by a public incident are set to the incident's impact at that minute.
Query param: `date` as Unix timestamp of the day's 00:00:00 UTC (seconds).
Returns all available roles.

Searches Services, Checks, Alerts, Incidents, Maintenances, On-Call Schedules, and Escalation
Policies by name/title/slug. Owner/Admin callers additionally get Users and API Keys in the results.
Returns a paginated list of services ordered by display_order, optionally filtered by name/slug search.

post.summary: Creates a new service.

get.summary: Returns a single service by its slug.

put.summary: Updates an existing service. Only provided fields are changed.

delete.summary: Deletes a service and all its checks.

post.summary:
Enqueues status recomputation for all services. Runs asynchronously through the same
channel check results use, so it serializes with other in-flight recomputations
instead of racing them with a direct read-modify-write.

Sends a verification code to the given address using not-yet-saved email settings,
proving the config actually works before anything is persisted. Stateless — the code is
an HMAC of the address, the exact config, and the current time window, verified the same
way on confirm. No account or config exists yet at this point in the wizard.
Confirms a verification code sent by Task<IActionResult> SetupController.SendEmailVerificationCode(SendSetupEmailCodeRequest request, CancellationToken ct).

get.summary: Returns whether initial setup is still required.

post.summary:
Completes first-run setup: creates Owner account, seeds roles,
and saves site + email configuration atomically.
Can only be called once — subsequent calls are rejected if an Owner already exists.

get.summary: Returns current site configuration. Public — used by the status page and sign-in page.

put.summary: Updates site text configuration fields.

post.summary: Uploads a site asset (logo | favicon | og-image). Stores in wwwroot/uploads/.

delete.summary: Removes a site asset (logo | favicon | og-image).

get.summary: Lists a service's own tags.

put.summary: Replaces a service's full user-tag set.

get.summary: Lists a check's own tags and its effective (inherited) tags.

put.summary: Replaces a check's full user-tag set.

get.summary: Lists a worker's own tags.

put.summary: Replaces a worker's full user-tag set.
Assigns (or sets the value of) an assignable system tag on a service.

delete.summary: Unassigns an assignable system tag from a service.

put.summary: Assigns (or sets the value of) an assignable system tag on a check.

delete.summary: Unassigns an assignable system tag from a check.

get.summary: Lists a check's required worker tags (Part B scheduling). Empty ⇒ the check runs on any worker.

put.summary: Replaces a check's required-worker-tag set. Rejected for single-region-only check types.

get.summary: Autocomplete: distinct user tag keys, optionally filtered by prefix.
Autocomplete: distinct values assigned for a given key.
Lists all users with their roles.

post.summary: Sends an email invitation to a new user.
Accepts an invitation and activates the account. No authentication required.

put.summary: Changes a user's role. Owner-only.

delete.summary: Deletes a user. Owner and Admin can delete non-Owner users.

get.summary: Returns a single user by ID.
Returns a user's personal notification preferences.

post.summary: Creates a new personal notification preference, appended at the lowest priority.

put.summary: Edits an existing personal notification preference's channel/integration/handle.

delete.summary: Deletes a personal notification preference. Rejects the account-fallback preference.

put.summary: Reorders a user's personal notification preferences.

post.summary: Sends a one-time verification code to an already-saved (pending) preference's handle.
Confirms the verification code for a pending preference.

get.summary: Returns all IANA timezones available on the server, sorted by UTC offset then name.
Returns all registered workers with their live connection state.

post.summary:
Registers a new remote worker and returns its token.
The token is shown exactly once — store it immediately as PIRO_WORKER_TOKEN.

Enables or disables the built-in API worker at runtime without restarting the application.
The setting is also persisted to the database so it survives restarts.

patch.summary: Updates mutable fields (region) of a worker registration.

delete.summary: Deletes a worker registration and invalidates its token.

SetupEmailConfigPayload.description:
The email config fields the verification code's HMAC is bound to — changing any of
    these after requesting a code invalidates it, so confirming proves this exact config works.

TestCheckRequest.description: Body for the check Test endpoint — the candidate config to test, or null to use the persisted one.

ApiKey.description: API key for programmatic access. Prefix: `pk_`.
ApiKey.name: X-API-Key
